newsitem.title: FRANCE: GBL TO UP SUEZ LYONNAISE STAKE.
newsitem.headline: GBL TO UP SUEZ LYONNAISE STAKE.

text.p: The merged group Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux plans to cut its stake in glass group Saint-Gobain, in line with its strategy of untangling cross shareholdings, Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet said.
Lyonnaise des Eaux and Cie de Suez on Friday said they planned to merge.

Jerome Monod, head of Lyonnaise and chairman designate of the supervisory board of the merged group, told an analysts meeting that Belgian businessman Albert Frere, who controls Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, aimed to bring his 5.3 pct stake in the merged group to the 8.3 percent he currently has in Suez.
Frere and his group will see their stake dilute to 5.3 percent as a result of the merger via a share-swap of Lyonnaise and Suez.
"Mister Frere has mentioned his intention to maintain, or even increase, his stake to keep a level that is not too far from what he had in Suez," Monod said.

Mestrallet said that the group would cut "in a symmetrical way" its four percent stake in Saint-Gobain after the chairman of the latter group, Jean-Louis Beffa, had said he wanted to cut his stake -- also some four percent -- in Suez.
